subject: Business
title: Currency Risk in Global Supply Chains
description: A micro-lesson that makes Currency Risk in Global Supply Chains usable.

hook.text: You agree to buy parts for 100 yen each. By delivery, the yen strengthens 15%. Your costs jump $150,000.

buildup.text: Currency risk means exchange rate fluctuations can change the actual cost of international transactions.

discovery.text: A 10% currency shift can erase an entire year's profit margin on an international deal.

twist.text: Companies use hedging — financial contracts that lock in exchange rates — to protect against swings.

climax.text: Airbus prices planes in dollars but incurs costs in euros. Currency management is as important as engineering.

punchline.text: In global trade, the exchange rate is the invisible price tag on everything.

quiz.question: How do companies protect against currency risk?
options: By hedging with financial contracts that lock in exchange rates
By only trading in their home currency
By storing large amounts of foreign cash

details.summary: Currency fluctuations create financial risk in global supply chains because purchases and sales occur in different currencies. Exchange rate movements can erode profit margins, change the relative cost of sourcing locations, and create unexpected gains or losses on outstanding contracts.
details.whyItMatters: A 10 percent currency shift can eliminate profit margins on international transactions. Managing currency risk through hedging, natural offsets, and contract terms is essential for maintaining predictable costs in global supply chains.
takeaways: Exchange rate movements alter the true cost of internationally sourced goods
Forward contracts lock in exchange rates to reduce future cost uncertainty
Natural hedging matches revenue and cost currencies to offset exposure

faq.question: How do companies hedge against currency risk in supply chains?
faq.answer: Forward contracts fix exchange rates for future transactions. Options provide protection while allowing benefit from favorable moves. Natural hedging sources inputs and sells outputs in the same currency. Invoice currency negotiation shifts risk between buyer and supplier.

faq.question: How can currency shifts change where companies source materials?
faq.answer: A strengthening dollar makes imports cheaper for US buyers, potentially favoring overseas suppliers. A weakening dollar makes imports more expensive, favoring domestic sources. Companies periodically reassess sourcing geography as exchange rates shift competitive advantages.
